solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Plant’s men rebuked in the past (6)

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, the ordinary soldiers
chid is the old past tense of chide

annotation.surface: A gardener's staff were told off long ago.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant's' reads as a factory's workforce; the 's is just 'is' joining the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the orchid is one family among flowering plants.

entries.clue: Authorised agents left behind inoperative insurgents at first (8)

indicatorNotes.behind: to be behind is to come after, so CIA and L follow OFF and I
indicatorNotes.at first: what comes at first in a word is its opening letter, here the I of insurgents

blocks.note: a machine that is off is not operating

annotation.surface: Licensed spies leave rebels behind, stranded and out of action.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Authorised agents' looks like a single phrase, but only the first word is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain adjective synonym: an official visit or result is one sanctioned by those in charge.

entries.clue: One leaves revolutionary Russian leader after tea in bed (7)

indicatorNotes.One leaves: one is I, and when it leaves LENIN the letters LENN remain
indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution is a full turn, so a revolutionary word is turned round: LENN becomes NNEL
indicatorNotes.after: placed after means written later, so NNEL follows CHA

blocks.note: Lenin led the Russian revolution; drop the I and turn the rest round

annotation.surface: A revolutionary leader lies in bed while someone slips out after tea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' seems to describe Lenin, which it fairly does, but its job is to turn LENN round. The definition is the last word: a river bed.
annotation.definitionFit: A less common sense of bed: the bed a river runs in is its channel.

entries.clue: Understand trainee contracted by sandwich shop (9)

indicatorNotes.contracted: something contracted has shrunk, so INTERN loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.by: by means beside, as in a house by the sea, so PRET sits next to INTER

blocks.note: an intern is a trainee; cut off the N
Pret A Manger is a British sandwich chain

annotation.surface: A trainee has signed a contract with a sandwich shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contracted by' reads as employed by, but 'contracted' shortens the trainee and 'by' just places the shop alongside. Pret A Manger is a sandwich chain found all over Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: to interpret a remark is to take it, or understand it, in a certain way.

entries.clue: The author’s explosive books coming very soon (8)

blocks.note: the author = the setter = I; I'm = I am
a mine is an explosive device
NT = New Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: A writer announces an explosive new book is on its way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The author's' means the setter speaking: I'm. 'Explosive books' reads as sensational titles but splits into two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym phrased as a paraphrase: an imminent storm is one about to break.

entries.clue: Emperor wrongly claims usurer steals gold (6,8)

indicatorNotes.wrongly: letters put down wrongly are out of their proper order, so CLAIMS USURER is rearranged
indicatorNotes.steals: a thief keeps stolen goods inside his coat, so the anagram takes AU inside it

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: A ruler falsely accuses a moneylender of stealing gold.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a courtroom scene with the emperor as judge; in fact the emperor is the answer and the usurer merely supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Marcus Aurelius ruled Rome from AD 161 to 180, the philosopher-emperor.

entries.clue: Bar in New York for locals avoided by poor actor (5)

indicatorNotes.avoided by: if the ham avoids Gotham he stays out of it, so HAM is taken out of GOTHAM

blocks.note: Gotham is a nickname for New York City
a ham is a bad, overacting actor; remove it

annotation.surface: A New York bar that regulars keep but a failing actor steers clear of.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar in New York' suggests a drinking place; the bar is a gold bar and 'in' is a piece of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Bar in its metal sense: an ingot is a cast block of gold or other metal.

entries.clue: Former temporary accommodation areas (7)

annotation.surface: A notice listing old sites of temporary housing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Former temporary accommodation' reads as a single phrase; only 'areas' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the extent of a forest is the area it covers.

entries.clue: Hurled professor’s chair (6)

indicatorNotes.professor’s: a professor is one who professes, declaring things out loud, so the professor's chair is the word as said

blocks.note: a throne is a chair of state

annotation.surface: An academic's chair has been flung across the room.
annotation.walkthrough: A professor's 'chair' is their post, which seems the whole point; the setter uses 'professor's' to mean the word as declared. The signal is loose, so lean on the crossers.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a ball thrown is a ball hurled.

entries.clue: Can clergyman definitely not put up bloke in flat? (6,8)

indicatorNotes.put up: in a down clue, putting something up raises it bottom to top, so NOSIR reads RISON
indicatorNotes.in: the pair are set in the flat, inside PLAIN

annotation.surface: Might a vicar refuse to give a lodger a room in his flat?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' opens the clue like a question, but it is slang for prison, and 'put up' pretends to mean giving someone a bed. 'No sir!' is a forceful refusal.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang in the definition: can is prison, so a can clergyman is the chaplain who ministers in a jail.

entries.clue: Sycophant judge turned to grab near the end (9)

indicatorNotes.turned: a word turned faces the other way, so REF reads FER
indicatorNotes.to grab: to grab is to seize and hold, so FER holds LATTER inside it

blocks.note: the latter part is the part near the end

annotation.surface: A fawning judge changes sides to seize something as the case closes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like part of the definition, but the definition is only 'Sycophant'; the judge is a referee.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sycophant wins favour by flattering the powerful.

entries.clue: Fish edging towards reptile in Everglades (5)

indicatorNotes.edging: an edging is a border, so GAR runs round the edges of TO

blocks.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

annotation.surface: A fish drifts nervously towards an alligator in a Florida swamp.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is one Florida scene, and the fish really is edging towards the reptile; 'edging' is doing the wrapping.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional word: gator is American shorthand for the alligators of the Florida swamps.

entries.clue: Rumours about informer briefly meeting senior officer (7)

indicatorNotes.briefly: said briefly means cut short, so NARK loses its K
indicatorNotes.meeting: things meeting come together end to end, so DS joins NAR

blocks.note: a nark is a police informer; lose the K

annotation.surface: Gossip spreads about a police informant meeting a senior detective.
annotation.walkthrough: The police surface keeps 'informer' and 'officer' looking like people in a story. A nark is British slang for a police informer.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowing from French: a canard (literally a duck) is a false or baseless rumour.

entries.clue: So far ahead, pull on clogs (2,2,3)

indicatorNotes.clogs: to clog a pipe is to block it from inside, so ON sits inside TOW

blocks.note: a team two up is ahead

annotation.surface: Well ahead so far, someone puts on wooden shoes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clogs' looks like footwear being pulled on; it is a verb, ON blocking up TOW.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom swapped for another: up to now and so far both mean until the present moment.

entries.clue: More competent Republican on board? Not initially (5)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it, so R follows TABLE
indicatorNotes.Not initially: without its initial means the first letter goes, so T is dropped

blocks.note: a board is a table, as in bed and board

annotation.surface: Would a Republican on the board be more capable?
annotation.walkthrough: 'On board' reads as joining a company; here R simply sits after TABLE before the T is dropped.
annotation.definitionFit: A comparative for a comparative: abler is more able, and able means competent.

entries.clue: Narrowly avoided collision — one arm is shaking, somewhat (4,4)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the phrase is taken

annotation.surface: After nearly crashing, a driver's arm is still trembling.
annotation.walkthrough: The trembling arm is exactly what a near miss leaves behind, which keeps the solver in the scene rather than reading the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the term comes from aviation and driving, where two vehicles nearly collide.

entries.clue: I act macho, stirring coffee (9)

indicatorNotes.stirring: stirring moves things around a cup, so the letters of I ACT MACHO are moved around

annotation.surface: A man swaggers while stirring his coffee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' belongs so naturally with coffee that it hides its job of mixing the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a macchiato is one kind of coffee, espresso with a dash of milk.

entries.clue: Artist sent Marx crazy (3,5)

indicatorNotes.crazy: crazy means disordered in the head, so the letters of SENT MARX are thrown into disorder

annotation.surface: A painter drove Karl Marx mad.
annotation.walkthrough: Marx points to philosophy; the artist is a surrealist, which suits a clue about madness.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Max Ernst was a German Dada and surrealist painter.

entries.clue: Prime minister, primarily Tory one who loathes cuddling children (8)

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter of Tory is used
indicatorNotes.cuddling: to cuddle is to hold in your arms, so HATER wraps round CH

blocks.note: ch = children, as in census forms

annotation.surface: A Tory leader is accused of loathing children even while hugging them.
annotation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was the Conservative (Tory) prime minister from 1979 to 1990, so the political surface points straight at her.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Margaret Thatcher held the office from 1979 to 1990.

entries.clue: Husband rather against emptying out home, naturally (7)

indicatorNotes.emptying out: a room emptied out keeps only its walls, so against keeps only its outer letters

blocks.note: a bit = rather, as in a bit cold

annotation.surface: A husband is reluctant to clear out the family home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Naturally' belongs to the definition: it narrows 'home' to the natural home of an animal or plant.
annotation.definitionFit: A qualified definition: 'naturally' turns home into the environment where a species lives in nature.

entries.clue: Accountant defending economic forecaster in emergency committee (5)

indicatorNotes.defending: defenders stand round what they guard, so CA surrounds OBR

blocks.note: the Office for Budget Responsibility, which forecasts the UK economy

annotation.surface: An accountant stands up for an economist before a crisis committee.
annotation.walkthrough: The OBR is the UK's official budget watchdog, which is why it counts as an economic forecaster.
annotation.definitionFit: A British proper name: COBRA, after Cabinet Office Briefing Room A, is where the government's crisis committee meets.

entries.clue: Boozy sessions with outspoken groups of girls (7)

indicatorNotes.outspoken: outspoken literally means spoken out, so the word is what you hear rather than what you read

blocks.note: a bevy is a group, especially of girls

annotation.surface: Frank-talking hen parties out on the town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outspoken' seems to describe the girls, and the whole scene is a rowdy night out.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: a bevvy is a drink, and also a drinking session.

entries.clue: Extremely polite Disney princess raised like princess in fairytale (6)

indicatorNotes.Extremely: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so polite gives P and E
indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raising lifts the letters bottom to top, so PEELSA reads upwards

annotation.surface: A very courteous Disney heroine was brought up like a fairytale princess.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for polite; it means the ends. The setter uses 'princess' twice on purpose: once in the wordplay, once in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by allusion: Sleeping Beauty lay asleep for a hundred years.

entries.clue: Reduce intoxication: live right, stopping liquid lunch? (5,2)

indicatorNotes.stopping: a stopper plugs a bottle's opening, so BE and R plug the middle of SOUP

blocks.note: soup is a lunch you drink
to be is to live, exist

annotation.surface: Advice to a drinker: live properly and quit the boozy lunches.
annotation.walkthrough: A liquid lunch usually means a lunch of alcohol, which fits the drinking theme; here it is soup.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb phrase for a verb phrase: to sober up is to become less drunk.

entries.clue: Country’s two rivers (5)

annotation.definitionNote: Country's is used as an adjective, of the countryside

blocks.note: the Ural is a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian Sea

annotation.surface: A nation is known for its two rivers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country' suggests a nation, but it means the countryside. One river is the abbreviation R, the other a named river.
annotation.definitionFit: A possessive standing for an adjective: the country's ways are rural ways, as opposed to the town's.

entries.clue: Briefly leave her fermenting port (2,5)

indicatorNotes.Briefly: said briefly means cut short, so leave loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.fermenting: fermenting liquid bubbles and churns, so the letters churn into a new order

annotation.surface: Leave her port wine to mature for a short while.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Port' next to 'fermenting' reads as the fortified wine; it is a French harbour city.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Le Havre is a major French seaport at the mouth of the Seine.

entries.clue: Key person agreeing to remove idiot (5)

indicatorNotes.to remove: to remove is to take away, so ASS comes out of ASSENTER

blocks.note: an ass is an idiot; take it away

annotation.surface: A crucial yes-man agrees to get rid of a fool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key person' reads as a vital figure; the key is on a keyboard.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Enter is one of the keys on a computer keyboard.

entries.clue: Notice you left case with no end of enthusiastic praise (9)

indicatorNotes.with no: a case with no C means ACTION without that letter
indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its final letter, so enthusiastic gives C

blocks.clueFragment: case with no end of enthusiastic
blocks.note: a court case is an action; remove the C that ends enthusiastic

annotation.surface: A notice saying you abandoned a case, unmoved by any glowing praise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Enthusiastic praise' reads as the definition, but 'enthusiastic' only supplies its final C.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: adulation is praise pushed to excess.

entries.clue: Impatient panel tut vigorously (8)

indicatorNotes.vigorously: something shaken vigorously is thoroughly jumbled, so PANEL TUT is rearranged

annotation.surface: An irritable committee tuts loudly in disapproval.
annotation.walkthrough: A tutting panel is exactly what petulance looks like, so the definition sits inside its own picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: petulant describes childish, irritable impatience.

entries.clue: My inflexible garment (6)

blocks.note: cor! and my! are both exclamations of surprise

annotation.surface: Someone complains about their stiff piece of clothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive but is the exclamation, as in 'My, that's tight!' Cor is British slang for the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a corset is a stiffened undergarment, and inflexible describes it well.
